en: The Apadāna of the Elder Dhajadāyaka Bījanīvagga, Chapter 8 [Verse 1] I was a merchant in the city of Benares, Possessing great wealth and abundant riches. Then, seeing the Buddha, the Great Sage, I offered him a victory banner. [Verse 2] Having made that offering of a victory banner, I attained the fruit of Stream-entry (sotāpatti). For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into the lower realms. [Verse 3] In every birth, wherever I was born, I possessed a beautiful, golden-colored body. And because I gave that gift of a victory banner, I have been reborn in the realm of the gods. [Verse 4] Now, having become a human being, I am free from all illness and disease. With a body like refined gold, I am honored by the world of men. [Verse 5] By the power of that merit, I have reached the final existence. Today, having seen the Buddha, the Great Sage, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship. [Verse 6] This is my final birth; There will be no further existence for me. Having cut off the stream of craving, I shall enter Parinibbāna. [Verse 7] The Buddha, the Great Sage, is my teacher; The Dhamma is my refuge. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I have crossed over the ocean of suffering. [Verse 8] I have paid homage to the Buddha, the Great Sage, Who is worthy of offerings and unsurpassed. Having heard his well-spoken words, I have attained the state of peace. [Verse 9] I have paid homage to the Dhamma, the Well-Spoken, Which leads to Nibbāna and is free from sorrow. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I have attained the state of peace. [Verse 10] I have paid homage to the Saṅgha, the Supreme Assembly, Of those who practice rightly and dwell in the right path. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I have attained the state of peace. [Verse 11] I have paid homage to the Elder Dhajadāyaka, Who has attained the state of peace and is free from defilements. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I have attained the state of peace. [Verse 12] I have paid homage to the Elder Dhajadāyaka, Who has abandoned birth and death and is free from sorrow. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I have attained the state of peace. [Verse 13] I have paid homage to the Elder Dhajadāyaka, Who has cut off the fetters and is free from bonds. Having heard the Dhamma from the Teacher, I have attained the state of peace. [Verse 14] I have paid homage to the Elder Dhajadāyaka, Who has transcended all suffering and is free from fear. “With a joyful heart, toward the supreme Bodhi tree of the Buddha Padumuttara,
I was filled with joy.”
I raised up a banner.
Having gathered the fallen leaves,
I discarded them outside.
Pure within and pure without,
resolute and free from taints—
just as if the Fully Awakened One were present before one's eyes.
I paid homage to the supreme Bodhi tree;
Padumuttara, the knower of the world,
the recipient of offerings.
Standing before the Saṅgha of bhikkhus,
the Teacher spoke these verses:
“By this gift of a banner, [may there be]...”
By attending upon both [parents],
for a hundred thousand eons he does not go to a state of misery.
Among the gods, he will experience no small divine splendor;
and many hundreds of times...
He will become a king in the realm;
known by the name Uggata,
he will be a wheel-turning monarch.
Having enjoyed prosperity,
impelled by the root of merit,
[he went] to the Blessed One Gotama.
He will find delight in the Teaching.
I am one who has exerted himself in striving,
calmed and free from acquisitions.
I bear my final body within the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
during the fifty-one thousand [years].
In a kappa, there was one named Uggata;
in fifty hundred thousand [kappas],
there was a kṣatriya named Megha.
The four analytical knowledges...
[and so forth] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Dhajadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Dhajadāyaka.
